identity.name: BRIDGE
identity.tagline: Cross-border mandate success starts with relational intelligence.
identity.description: A 36-item assessment that measures a leader's readiness to succeed in cross-border APAC mandates across six interconnected dimensions of relational and execution capability. Leaders receive a composite mandate readiness score, dimension-level verdicts, a primary archetype identifying their highest-risk failure pattern, and personalised development guidance.
identity.ideal_use_case: Pre-appointment assessment for APAC cross-border leadership roles; existing mandate health check; expatriate and local-national leader development; succession planning for China/APAC regional leadership roles.

instrument_spec.delivery_format: Online self-assessment with instant HTML report + consultant debrief
instrument_spec.scoring_method: Dimension-level normalised scores (0–20 each) + composite percentile (0–100)

dimensions.name: Mandate Clarity
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's specific, detailed understanding of what their mandate actually requires — including success criteria, stakeholder expectations, organisational history, and the 2–3 things that, if wrong in the first 90 days, make recovery much harder.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader has had direct conversations with principals about success, understands the mandate's distinguishing features, and can identify the critical early risks.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader's understanding is general rather than specific; they expect clarity to emerge over time rather than seeking it proactively at the outset.

dimensions.name: Stakeholder Relationship Building
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's ability to identify, invest in, and maintain key stakeholder relationships in high-context APAC environments — including informal power structures, relationship brokers, and government stakeholders — before those relationships are needed for specific transactions.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader invests in relationships proactively, reads informal power structures accurately, and maintains stakeholder relationships through tension and misalignment.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader defaults to transactional relationship-building, underestimates the importance of pre-investment, and may struggle to identify who has real influence.

dimensions.name: Communication Alignment
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's ability to adapt their natural communication style for APAC contexts — including directness, assertiveness, delivery of difficult messages, reading silence and indirection, and checking for genuine alignment rather than assuming agreement from the absence of objection.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader has adapted their communication style deliberately, checks for understanding, can deliver difficult messages effectively, and reads non-verbal cues as information.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader defaults to their natural style under pressure, may create friction through unadapted directness, and may mistake silence for agreement.

dimensions.name: Pressure Resilience
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's ability to sustain decision quality and mandate focus under the simultaneous pressures of headquarters expectations, local team dynamics, and market conditions — including recovery from relationship setbacks and early-warning self-awareness.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader's decision quality holds under sustained pressure, they recover quickly from setbacks, and they have personal early-warning systems for performance degradation.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader becomes more risk-averse under political pressure, struggles with prolonged uncertainty, and may not notice their own performance degradation until it is visible to others.

dimensions.name: Long-Game Thinking
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's comfort with investing in relationships and trust-building over 3–5 year timelines without immediate transactional return, and their ability to resist short-term pressure that would erode long-term relationship capital.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader prioritises long-term relationship trust over short-term wins, operates comfortably within multi-year trust-building cycles, and has a track record of sacrificing short-term results for long-term relationship health.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader is uncomfortable with delayed returns, focuses on near-term results under pressure, and may deplete relationship capital without noticing until damage is done.

dimensions.name: Cultural Fluency
dimensions.description: Measures the leader's specific understanding of cultural norms (hierarchy, consensus, face-saving, relationship-first communication) in their target APAC market, their ability to recover from cultural missteps, and the depth of their genuine cross-cultural relationships.
dimensions.what_high_means: The leader has current, specific cultural knowledge, understands how decisions are made in context, has repaired relationships after cultural missteps, and has built genuine mutual cross-cultural relationships.
dimensions.what_low_means: The leader treats cultural differences as friction to overcome, assumes their default leadership style is culturally compatible, and may have primarily transactional rather than genuine cross-cultural relationships.

archetype_framework.logic: Each archetype is defined by the leader's lowest-scoring dimension. The Cultural Operator is an exception profile: no dimension below 50th percentile AND Cultural Fluency above 70th percentile.

risk_layers.description: Risk arising from misaligned expectations and insufficient stakeholder connection. Associated with Mandate Clarity and Stakeholder Relationship Building weaknesses.
Risk arising from communication friction and performance degradation under pressure. Associated with Communication Alignment and Pressure Resilience weaknesses.
Risk arising from short-term orientation and insufficient cultural depth. Associated with Long-Game Thinking and Cultural Fluency weaknesses.

archetypes.name: The Envoy
archetypes.core_pattern: Great on paper, fails in practice because relationships don't form. The mandate dies from isolation.
growth_areas: Treats relationship-building as transactional rather than strategic
Underestimates how much time and patience APAC stakeholder relationships require
May fail to identify informal power structures and key relationship brokers
archetypes.development_focus: Invest in relationship-building before it is needed; develop structured stakeholder mapping including informal influence networks; approach government and institutional stakeholders with the same patience as commercial stakeholders.

archetypes.name: The Wanderer
archetypes.core_pattern: Misunderstands what the role actually requires. Misaligned expectations create early friction.
growth_areas: Assumes mandate clarity will emerge over time rather than proactively seeking it
May not have had direct success-definition conversations with principals
Risk of executing efficiently on the wrong priorities
archetypes.development_focus: Conduct explicit success-definition conversations with all key principals within the first 30 days; identify the 2–3 make-or-break factors for the first 90 days; build an organisational history and stakeholder politics map.

archetypes.name: The Chameleon
archetypes.core_pattern: Says all the right things in the wrong way. Message is right but delivery creates friction.
growth_areas: Natural communication style (directness, assertiveness, debate orientation) creates friction in APAC contexts
Reverts to default style under pressure, undoing adaptive efforts
May mistake silence for agreement and miss real alignment signals
archetypes.development_focus: Build specific adaptive communication techniques for APAC contexts; practice delivering difficult messages in culturally effective ways; develop active checking-for-understanding habits rather than assuming alignment from silence.

archetypes.name: The Anchor
archetypes.core_pattern: Starts strong, deteriorates under sustained pressure. The mandate doesn't fail in good times — it fails in the first crisis.
growth_areas: Decision quality degrades under simultaneous pressure from HQ, local team, and market
Becomes more risk-averse when the mandate becomes politically difficult
May not have early-warning systems for personal performance degradation
archetypes.development_focus: Identify personal pressure triggers and early-warning indicators; build specific coping strategies for each high-pressure pattern; develop recovery routines after relationship setbacks or political shocks.

archetypes.name: The Sprinter
archetypes.core_pattern: Wins short-term results but burns long-term relationship capital. The board sees Q1 wins and doesn't notice the damage.
growth_areas: Prioritises short-term results over long-term relationship health
Uncomfortable with 3–5 year relationship investment timelines
May deplete relationship capital faster than they realise, with delayed consequences
archetypes.development_focus: Build explicit long-horizon relationship investment plans; identify specific short-term pressures that create long-term damage; develop reputation-conscious decision frameworks for quarterly results pressure.

archetypes.name: The Cultural Operator
archetypes.weakest_dimension: No dimension below 50th percentile; Cultural Fluency above 70th percentile
archetypes.core_pattern: The ideal BRIDGE profile. Strong across all dimensions with cultural fluency as a demonstrated strength.
strengths: Balanced capability across all six mandate dimensions
Cultural fluency as a demonstrated strength, not just baseline competence
Genuine mutual cross-cultural relationships rather than one-directional adaptation
growth_areas: Risk of complacency — strong all-around scores can mask specific sub-threshold weaknesses
May underestimate the rate at which new cross-border challenges emerge
May need to develop mentorship capability to help build cultural fluency in others
archetypes.development_focus: Use cultural fluency as a platform for mentoring others; identify nuanced or emerging cultural shifts that may not yet be visible in standard assessment; develop advanced cross-border influence capabilities.

composite_scoring.method: Six-dimension average of normalised scores, converted to 0–100 composite

bands.interpretation: Strong readiness across all 6 dimensions; mandate risk is low.
Solid foundation with specific dimensions requiring attention. Proactive development recommended.
Multiple dimensions require deliberate investment before mandate effectiveness can be expected. Early intervention critical.
Significant gaps across mandate dimensions. Without targeted support, mandate failure probability is high.

dimension_verdicts.meaning: Emerging mandate capability with targeted development needs
